messages:
maria: Hey team — running into a weird combo of issues while trying to get the Redwood JS/TS SDK working in our Next.js sample app (app router). Goal: ESM build on edge runtime + server/client boundary. Steps I followed: installed @redwood/inference@latest, used the example from quickstart, and then tried to import server-only helpers in a server component. Errors below.
kevin: Paste the error?
maria: Server runtime throws: "SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module" when bundling for edge. Also client-side hydration complaining about `window` usage from the SDK's auth helper. Full trace: 
```
/var/task/.next/server/app/page.js: Unexpected token 'import'
 at Module._compile (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js: ...)
```
olivia: Sounds like a packaging mismatch (CJS vs ESM). Which export did you import? `const { createClient } = require('@redwood/inference')` vs `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'` matters for edge.
maria: I was using the README example which shows `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'`. But the package on npm still ships a CJS main + an `exports` field that is weird for edge. Next's edge runtime expects pure ESM for server components.
kevin: We ran into this in the sample app PR last quarter. Short workaround: dynamic import inside a server-only module, and guard so it never hits client bundle. Example:
```
// app/redwoodClient.server.ts
export async function getRedwoodClient() {
 const mod = await import('@redwood/inference/dist/esm/client.mjs')
 return mod.createClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY })
}
```
Then call from server components only.
maria: That helped for bundling, but now the auth helper (it tries refreshing tokens with fetch) fails in edge because it depends on `node:crypto` for JWK verification. Edge runtime doesn't have that.
olivia: Ah — that's an SDK parity issue. We have a node-first auth implementation and a browser/edge shim is missing. We need a lightweight edge-compatible path that uses Web Crypto and AbortSignal, etc.
sam: From product/ops side — this is causing onboarding friction in the sample app. New users copy the quickstart and hit cryptic errors. We should prioritize a fix: publish a dual entrypoint where package.json exports `./edge.mjs` for edge-compatible runtime and `./node.cjs` for node. Also document recommended imports for Next server components vs client.
kevin: Agreed. Short-term: update quickstart README with explicit note "for Next.js app router on the Edge runtime use dynamic import and the edge entrypoint" and provide the dynamic import snippet.
maria: Also typings: TS complains that the `.server.ts` dynamic import returns `any` because we point to a .mjs. Can we add types-only ESM export or a .d.ts alongside dist/esm/client.mjs? That would avoid `any` and improve DX.
olivia: yes add `types` field in package.json pointing to dist/types/index.d.ts and ship `dist/types`.
dev-bot: Deploy checklist: create GH issue for "edge runtime ESM entrypoint + webcrypto auth shim"; link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/issues/placeholder
maria: I'll open the issue and add failing repro steps and a small Next 14 app reproduction. For now I'm going to patch the sample app in our docs to use the dynamic import + server-only wrapper and a note about env var secrets not leaking to client.
kevin: Thanks — once issue is opened ping me and I'll attach the runtime tests we used for Deno/Cloudflare compatibility.
sam: Heads-up for the docs team: add a short table: runtime -> recommended import -> notes (edge/serverless vs node/dedicated). This will save a ton of support time.
maria: Appreciate it. If anyone has a minimal repro that's smaller than full Next app, drop it here and I'll try to trim and paste in the issue.
olivia: I'll paste a tiny repro gist later today. :+1:
